scored.reason: The flavour's hinge word is 'a better trigger' — a firearm. MORPHIVORE has no weapons, ranged or otherwise; a Clash Blue Alpha kills with limbs, teeth and mass, and the house voice hits the same idea through anatomy ('The good eye gone milky at the edges'). Swap the trigger for something the creature actually owns: a throw, a lunge, a stone it spits, distance it keeps. Secondly, 'Deadeye of the Molten Maw' is epic-title register — the 'X of the Y' construction plus 'Molten Maw' reads as a boss nameplate from a different genre, where this game names things by what they look and smell like ('Half mud, half meat, all squeal.'). 'Molten' also points at Volcanic while the subject is Blue, so the name argues with the family it belongs to. Formatting is clean: 14 words, one sentence, no exclamation, no 'This is a' opener, and the 'you're inside its arms' second person is the shipped kind (implicated predator), not instruction.
scored.was_flavor: One good eye and a better trigger; useless the second you're inside its arms.
scored.name: Deadeye Stonelobber
scored.flavor: One good eye and a better throw; useless the second you're inside its arms.

scored.reason: The flavour line is close to shipped quality — 'Slinks in, bites once, forgets to leave a body.' is eight words, one sentence, concrete violence with a dry joke in the tail, and it matches the rhythm of 'Rolls downhill faster than it ever runs uphill.' The name sinks it. 'Nightthroat of the Molten Maw' is boss-title grandeur: the 'X of the Y' epithet construction plus 'Molten Maw' is the epic/reverent register the GDD explicitly rules out, and 'Nightthroat' is atmospheric mood rather than meat, bone or appetite. Since form names carry the entire authorial voice, an honorific title is a heavier breach here than it looks. A Clash Purple Alpha in this game would be named for the body doing the eating — something blunt and anatomical along the lines of 'Bruisegullet' or 'Hot-Throat Purple' — not given a fantasy epithet. Drop 'of the Molten Maw' entirely and make the head-word physical.

scored.reason: The flavour line is excellent house voice — 'Doesn't have a weak side, and hates that you keep looking for one.' is concrete, unsentimental, quietly funny, and sits right in the shipped rhythm and length. The name is the problem: 'Greytyrant of the Molten Maw' is an epic boss-title construction, and the '<Name> of the <Adjective> <Noun>' epithet is exactly the reverent register C1 bans. 'Tyrant' imports a throne and a realm to overthrow, which contradicts GDD §1 ('you are not saving anything, you are trying to sit on top') — an Alpha is just the biggest thing eating in that biome, not a ruler. 'the Molten Maw' also invents a proper-noun location; this game's geography is Prairies, Wetlands, Mountains, Beach, Volcanic, and nothing else is named. Fix: keep the Grey family marker and the mouth, drop the coronation — something built from meat, heat and appetite ('Greychar Gullet', 'Slaghide Chewer') rather than a title granted by a kingdom that doesn't exist.
scored.was_flavor: Doesn't have a weak side, and hates that you keep looking for one.
scored.name: Greychar Gullet
scored.flavor: Crusted grey the whole way round, no soft belly to bite, and a breath like burnt fat.

scored.reason: The name 'The Main Course' is good crude food-chain comedy and the vocabulary is clean — 'biomes' is this game's noun and nothing foreign creeps in. The flavour is the problem. 'You spent five biomes learning how to eat' is a progression victory-lap: abstract, retrospective, congratulatory, and it summarises the run rather than describing a body. The house voice never audits the player's journey; it points at meat ('Half mud, half meat, all squeal.') or at a specific violent moment ('pried out with your knee on its chest'). Replace the summary with something physical about a Clash Grey apex — jaw, gristle, what's still stuck in its teeth. Second problem: the referent flips mid-line. Sentence one addresses 'You', sentence two says 'Nothing has ever eaten it back' — the form is 'you' and then suddenly 'it'. Pick one and hold it ('Nothing has ever eaten you back.').
scored.was_flavor: You spent five biomes learning how to eat. Nothing has ever eaten it back.
scored.name: The Main Course
scored.flavor: Jaw crusted with gristle it never bothered to swallow. Nothing has ever eaten it back.
